SOL OBSERVABLE SEPARATION V3 — LINEAR ENTROPY TRANSFER FOR TIME-SYMMETRIC TESTS
9 October 2026. Append-only mathematical improvement to v1/v2. The finite witness, coefficient artifact, and sampling cost are unchanged. No novelty or external validation claim.

RESULT
The seven-letter statistic w in v1 is pointwise invariant under reversing its observation window. This symmetry permits the stronger dimension/rate-independent entropy-production certificate
  sigma >= -(2/T) log(1-delta/2) >= delta/T,
where T=2(t+h)=.002000000002 and delta=1/(6*10^45).
Consequently every stationary finite physically-even CTMC with this observed process has
  sigma >8.333333325*10^(-44) nats per model time unit,
and in particular sigma>6*10^(-44).
The earlier >2*10^(-89) bound remains valid but is superseded quantitatively. Acquisition still requires approximately 1.1*10^93 independent stationary windows at the displayed worst-case confidence guarantee.

1. PATH HELLINGER DOMINATION LEMMA
Let Q be any finite stationary CTMC on the support of pi, and Q* its stationary adjoint. Assume all hidden variables are physically even. Let S=(Q+Q*)/2. Write p,q,s for the stationary path densities of Q,Q*,S on [0,T] with respect to a common path-skeleton/time reference measure. For finite entropy production, reverse edges share support; infinite entropy production makes every finite lower bound automatic.

Stationarity gives the same escape rate lambda_i for Q and Q* at every hidden state. S has the same escape rate. Their path densities therefore share the initial factor pi_(x0) and integrated holding factor exp(-integral lambda_(X_u)du). Only the jump factors differ. On every path,
  sqrt(p q)
    =pi_(x0) exp(-integral lambda) product_jumps sqrt(Q_ij Q*_ij)
    <=pi_(x0) exp(-integral lambda) product_jumps [(Q_ij+Q*_ij)/2]
    =s,                                                        (H1)
by edgewise arithmetic-geometric mean. This is pointwise path-density domination, not an assertion that Q* and Q trajectories have a common transition kernel.

Put r=sqrt(pq), m=(p+q)/2, and A=integral r. Both m-r and s-r are nonnegative, and each integrates to 1-A. Hence
  TV(m,s)=(1/2)integral |m-s|
    <=(1/2)integral[(m-r)+(s-r)]=1-A.                    (H2)
For finite path KL, Jensen under p gives
  A=E_p exp[-(1/2)log(p/q)]
    >=exp[-D(p||q)/2]=exp[-T sigma/2].                  (H3)
Here D(p||q)=T

SOL HIDDEN REALIZATION V4 — FINITE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE AND FINAL STATUS
9 October 2026. Append-only addendum; v1-v3 remain frozen.

The root-assigned distinct Sol continuation has closed the existential operational gate in v2 Section7. Its full proof is work/sol/observable_separation/v1.txt-v3.txt; exact rational coefficients are witness_rational_v1.json and the standard-library generator/checker is build_and_verify_witness_v1.py. The evaluator evaluate_witness_v1.py reads only that coefficient file and observed words/counts, without reading hidden-state data or the source generator.

There is one fixed rational statistic of the seven observed letters at
  -t-h,-t,-h,0,h,t,t+h,
  h=10^(-12), t=1/1000,
whose unnormalized expectation is >=0 for every stationary reversible hidden Markov process with deterministic emissions under the stated standard conditional-feature assumptions, and <-10^(-6) for the exact ten-state process in v2. Its pointwise absolute value is <6*10^39. Thus normalizing gives a gap delta=1/(6*10^45).

The statistic is pointwise time-reversal-even. A separately proved path-affinity comparison yields, for every stationary finite all-even CTMC exact completion,
  sigma>=-(2/T)log(1-delta/2)>=delta/T,
  T=2(t+h),
  delta/T=1/[12*1000000001*10^33]>8.333333325*10^(-44).
The conservative floor sigma>6*10^(-44) is therefore certified. This improves the still-valid Pinsker floor >2*10^(-89). The complete new transfer proof is in observable_separation/v3 and my independent observable_audit_v2.

I independently reconstructed the finite conditional-feature, polygon, circle-defect, symmetric-coupling, rounding, Young-penalty, and target-error estimates. My separate standard-library exact audit is observable_audit_v1.py. It and Sol7's generator agree on raw witness upper bound -1.173761546566417e-6 and pointwise bound 4.9612680000577e39<6e39. Frozen audits observable_audit_v1.txt-v2.txt preserve the complete reconstruction and its limitations.

The displayed acquisition guarantee uses approximately 1.0624*10^93 independent stationary windows at 95-percent confidence and temporal resolution 10^(-12). This is a sufficient worst-case Hoeffding cost, not a lower bound on every algorithm. No uniform single-trajectory mixing guarantee, useful experimental efficiency, optimal dissipation estimate, or empirical confirmation is claimed.

FOCUSED PRIORITY FOLLOW-UP — 9 October 2026
This is a limited live source comparison, not a proof of novelty or a literature-completeness claim.

Jorgensen, Neeb and Olafsson, Reflection Positive Stochastic Processes Indexed by Lie Groups, arXiv:1510.07445v3, https://arxiv.org/html/1510.07445v3 . Read Definition3.4, Proposition3.7 and the Markov characterization in Theorem3.27. Standard positivity requires a positivity-preserving semigroup on an actual L-infinity lattice. The Markov reconstruction has an additional cyclicity condition. The present common-atom reflected Gram representation is static and does not supply such an invariant lattice or reversible transition kernel. Gaussian second quantization of a selfadjoint contraction also does not preserve the required finite-label emission products. Thus these reconstruction statements do not automatically invalidate or establish the ten-state counterexample. Approximately 100 words of substantive source-derived comparison here; no text quoted.

Boyle and Petersen, Hidden Markov Processes in the Context of Symbolic Dynamics, source PDF https://petersen.web.unc.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/17054/2018/04/06Jan2010.pdf . Used only to locate the historical Heller/Dharmadhikari realization lineage and reversible lumpability references; this is a survey rather than the primary proof. Its reversible reference concerns when an observed function of a Markov process remains Markov, a different question from existence of an arbitrary equilibrium hidden completion. No novelty conclusion follows. The original Heller and Burke-Rosenblatt papers were not fully inspected by this root follow-up.

Search terms included reversible hidden Markov realization, reflection positivity, completely positive equilibrium process, positive realization, detailed balance lifting, and finite-rank Markov semigroup. No identical all-word-CP/outside-unrestricted-equilibrium-cylinder-closure theorem was identified in this limited search. That negative search result is not historical-priority evidence.
